builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: When All Rollouts Fail: Policy-Compatible Joint Decoding for Hard-Problem Reasoning
summary: PICO replaces standard RLVR methods (e.g., GRPO, RLOO) and direct expert-trajectory imitation for hard problems where all on-policy rollouts fail, by generating verified, policy-compatible trajectories via distribution-constrained joint decoding and optimizing them with a mixed-behavior objective. It requires access to expert data, increases training-time complexity and computational cost due to joint decoding and importance sampling corrections, and demands careful tuning of a divergence budget and dynamic top-k. The approach can fail if expert data are unavailable, unrepresentative, or too far from the student policy, if the divergence budget is mis-set, or if importance sampling introduces high variance that destabilizes learning.
rationale: The method targets a specific failure mode of RLVR and may improve reasoning quality, but it requires expert data, additional decoding machinery, and RL training capacity that are difficult to justify for a single-GPU, small-team production setting without further validation.
technique: Policy-Compatible Reinforcement Learning (PICO) for Hard Reasoning

claims.statement: PICO replaces standard RLVR methods (e.g., GRPO, RLOO) and direct expert-trajectory imitation for hard problems where all on-policy rollouts fail, by generating verified, policy-compatible trajectories via distribution-constrained joint decoding and optimizing them with a mixed-behavior objective. It requires access to expert data, increases training-time complexity and computational cost due to joint decoding and importance sampling corrections, and demands careful tuning of a divergence budget and dynamic top-k. The approach can fail if expert data are unavailable, unrepresentative, or too far from the student policy, if the divergence budget is mis-set, or if importance sampling introduces high variance that destabilizes learning.

The paper states that PICO 'consistently outperforms standard RLVR and prior off-policy baselines' across reasoning and agentic benchmarks, but provides no quantified improvement factor in the abstract.
